Converting geographically indexed tables

Source: vignettes/pg_from_table.Rmd
pg_from_table.Rmd
library(priogridR)

pg_from_table() is designed for values stored in a table and indexed by geographic units such as countries, districts, or administrative regions. It joins the table to matching polygons and transfers the values to PRIO-GRID.

Example geography and table 

make_rectangle <- function(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) {
  sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(
    c(
      xmin, ymin,
      xmax, ymin,
      xmax, ymax,
      xmin, ymax,
      xmin, ymin
    ),
    ncol = 2,
    byrow = TRUE
  )))
}

districts <- sf::st_sf(
  district_id = c("A", "B"),
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(
    make_rectangle(5, 15, 45, 55),
    make_rectangle(15, 25, 45, 55),
    crs = 4326
  )
)

population <- data.frame(
  district_id = c("A", "B"),
  population_total = c(100000, 150000)
)

config <- priogrid::pg_config(
  nrow = 18,
  ncol = 36,
  start_date = as.Date("2020-12-31"),
  end_date = as.Date("2021-12-31"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

source_id identifies rows in the table, while geography_id identifies the matching polygons.

population_pg <- pg_from_table(
  x = population,
  variable = "population",
  value = "population_total",
  geography = districts,
  source_id = "district_id",
  geography_id = "district_id",
  aggregation = "area_weighted_sum",
  config = config
)

head(population_pg)
#>   pgid population
#> 1  487   26308.96
#> 2  488   65772.40
#> 3  489   39463.44
#> 4  523   23691.04
#> 5  524   59227.60
#> 6  525   35536.56

Choosing a transfer rule

Three rules are available:

  • area_weighted_sum allocates a source-unit total in proportion to polygon overlap with each cell. This is appropriate for totals such as population when uniform spatial distribution is an acceptable assumption.
  • area_weighted_mean weights source values by their overlap area in each target cell. This is suitable for rates or continuous attributes.
  • constant assigns the source value without proportional allocation and is appropriate when the attribute is understood to apply throughout the source polygon.

These rules encode different assumptions. Area weighting does not account for within-polygon population distribution, land use, or other spatial heterogeneity unless that information is supplied separately.

Repeated observations and time

Use time_column when the table contains observations for multiple dates. Each date is mapped to an interval in the supplied configuration.

population_by_year <- data.frame(
  district_id = rep(c("A", "B"), 2),
  observation_date = as.Date(c(
    "2020-12-31", "2020-12-31", "2021-12-31", "2021-12-31"
  )),
  population_total = c(100000, 150000, 102000, 153000)
)

population_time <- pg_from_table(
  x = population_by_year,
  variable = "population",
  value = "population_total",
  geography = districts,
  source_id = "district_id",
  geography_id = "district_id",
  time_column = "observation_date",
  aggregation = "area_weighted_sum",
  config = config
)

Before conversion, check for duplicate table keys, unmatched identifiers, and invalid polygon geometries. Only identifiers present in both inputs are retained by the join.

See vignette("pg_from_vector", package = "priogridR") for direct polygon conversion and additional aggregation rules.
